reviews.excerpt: Great professor if you really want to understand the subject. Teaches a lot from the chalkboard, but he does record and post all his lectures, so there's a lot of flexibility there.
She makes the subject matter really straight forward. Lectures are very clear, and she always posts class notes.
This class is so chill! There are four midterms that you take in lecture and five quizzes that you take in discussion.
Very nice and helpful professor. He will stay after class to answer questions, but his lectures are extremely boring.
Decent professor. Uploads lecture notes to elms after lectures. His notes are pretty reflective of the textbook.
Super good lecturer who genuinely cares. Quizzes are much easier than the exams, although the homework does take a while.
She is a very considerate professor and wants you to succeed. Her worksheets and quizzes were very reasonable and not difficult at all.
You can't really ask for much more out of a Calc 2 professor. He posts notes after every lecture and has weekly surveys so you can let him know what was going well and what wasn't.
The absolute best. Explains concepts very clearly and shows that she really cares about the students that she teaches during discussion.
Probably closer to 3.5 stars. Lectures are kind of boring and hard to pay attention to because he’s kind of monotone, but he’s super organized.
Very good professor who records lectures and posts the slides on ELMS.
This course was significantly more difficult than other sections of the same course due to the instructor's exam design and grading policies.
This class was a genuine disaster. None of the study material ever matched the content on the tests or quizzes.
His lectures and slides were very good. The projects are extremely detailed and very useful for understanding the content.
I second that the exam averages for all the midterms were low (around 60s) but to me it didn't really affect me.
Her lectures aren't perfect like others have mentioned, but her slides and code examples are really good for learning the content.
Hard class with no curve. English 101 and this course will have the same grading breakdown.
Teaches well and is very clear on what is expected in the exams, projects, and worksheets.
Amazing professor! All lectures are recorded, exams are graded fairly, labs encourage group work and actual learning.
Amazing Professor! Lectures are very engaging and he explains things clearly.
Really well ran course. The projects were pretty instructive, especially the Assembly project.
He is a really good professor with a joy for teaching. All you have to do is come to class and submit the assignments.
Took her last fall, she was genuinely amazing. Homework probably took a grand total of 20 seconds per week, and in class exercises were super fun and engaging.
Very chill teacher, gave a lot of class time for the assignments.
Super easy professor. He made the course super easy to follow along and graded assignments very easily.
It was her first semester teaching native English speakers, so she was probably more lenient with grading.
While the rubrics and instructions for the assignments can be confusing, and she isn’t great at answering questions, the class isn’t bad.
I had his class for FC at 4:30-5:45pm. Assignments are in order and neat.
Just a lot of busy work that isn’t relevant to the big writing assignments and takes forever to grade the big writing assignments.
Honestly, you could pass this class without going to the lectures and just reading his slides.
Great Professor! Records lectures and is very approachable. Class doesn’t require too much time, but you do have to stay on top of your work.
Overall great professor and great class. He teaches you how to study for exams and what specific content/sections will be covered.
He is a great storyteller, but an improvable professor. My points are the same as those of the other who rate him low, you cannot expect too much exam content from class.
I think she is a good professor and the exams were fair. There are 3 exams and then an optional final that could replace a low exam grade.
She was nice, classes are on zoom and you are allowed to bring a piece of paper 8x11 to the exams.
I am an economics major with 0 economic background in high school and currently have a 95 in the class before finals.
Stopped attending his lectures because of tedious and less retaining lectures.
She just doesn't explain things all that well , and also assigns graded assignments before covering that topic in class.
I'm not sure why his ratings are so low. His exams are actually pretty manageable—they’re all multiple choice, and there are only three total exams (two midterms and a final).
The whole class is asynchronous and on your own pace. There are three problem sets, a midterm exam, and a final exam.
If you did well on ECON200, you won’t really need to attend lecture for about the first half of the course.
He is clearly very passionate about what he is teaching about but it is hard to understand in lecture.
On the second exam, the class average was a failing grade. This was a direct result of the professor failing to provide study material relevant to the questions on the exam.
In the second half of the semester, he got so much better. His midterm 2 was really good and he gave us a practice exam that was very similar to the actual exam.
She taught really well. The exams were very fair and similar to what you'd find on the homework and practice exams.
Assignments are almost free 100's, so it's down to the exams, which aren't too bad if you know your calculus (and can be bothered to study).
He's not a very good lecturer, and his notes are confusing to read. The quizzes are pretty simple and the exams are okay since he posts the practice problems.
Lectures are just reading off textbook definition. However, he is nice and answers to quizzes are given before taking it.
Great professor! She is super nice and keeps her lectures engaging. Discussions are straightforward generally composed of a small quiz to review that week’s material.
She is a very caring professor and wants the best for her students. Like others mentioned, her practice exams were very similar to her actual ones (except for the last exam).
To be honest, the exams are weighted very heavily, but he's very generous with the grading system, which is technically his version of a curve.
While she is an enjoyable teacher and attempts to keep her lectures fun, she definitely has some glaring issues.
Very nice. Class is not difficult and practice exams are very similar to actual exams.
Found her lecture style to fit my style of learning very well. She was very nice and used lots of non-chemistry examples to help you understand the material.
I really liked her, she taught very well and the homework really connected to the concepts we learned in class.
A really great professor who did a great job of making the material understandable and providing many ways to review/practice.
Canvas is a little unorganized and yes the reflection quizzes are hard, but your experience really depends on how good your TA is.
He never covers topics that are on the homework and his exams are ridiculously hard.
If you are going to take BSCI 170, you really should take this class-- she gives worksheets a week before the exam, and the worksheet is literally copied and pasted onto the exam.
This class was incredibly easy. The exams were easy, not sure why people are complaining.
Loves his job, explains things well and records lectures so you can go back if you don't understand the first time.
There is a lot of material in this class and going through 70-80 slides per lecture is a lot to digest.
She goes through lecture slides super fast but there isn't much work and it is pretty easy.
I really liked him. He kept the lectures interesting and fun which is hard for a class like physics.
She is a pretty good professor. She doesn't make the lecture particularly boring but neither are they too exciting.
Took this course over the summer and overall a good professor. Quizzes were easy, exams were fair.
He is a very monotone speaker making lectures very boring but his style of teaching is very good.
Expect to learn more from the textbook than you do him. He is not good at explaining topics and when he decides to give out examples he just uses variables and only does half a problem.
Fairly easy class, especially if you took AP computer science. Consists of three-ish short projects with weekly homework.
He was a nice person. However, he would take a very long time to grade stuff which was very stressful and annoying because the assignments would build off of each other.
Much of the material learned was complicated, and a lot of the people in the class had a lot of advanced prior coding knowledge and were able to complete assignments without much worry.
His lectures are very engaging, and you can tell he is very knowledgeable about the subject he teaches.
Honestly, a great professor. You don't really need to go to the lectures, as he posts all the slides online, but the lectures are pretty interesting to attend.
Decent professor, is understanding about assignments and their time, not a bad choice for ENES 100.
She is a really really nice professor. Grading was usually very good and assignments were usually fun.
Not a great lecturer, but he is a very chill teacher. Only problem is that he is very strict with grading.
Super nice and sweet teacher but harsh and very meticulous in grading.
